messages:
alex_cheng: Heads up 026-03-17 customer org_8YxN called in with a weird 'staircase' p99 on /v1/embeddings after the recent batcher tuning. Putting logs and repro here.

maya_garcia: Please paste tenant + sample request + any HTTP errors you've observed (400/504/429).

alex_cheng: tenant=org_8YxN. Repro curl we used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ 
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
 -d '{"model":"embed-1024","input":["short","a much longer text sample", "..."]}'
```
Server logs show usual dynbatch flush ~100ms but intermittent long flushes ~700-900ms recurring ~every 10m. Excerpt:
```
[dynbatch] flush window=100ms batch_size=128 reason=max_batch
[serve] kvcache_evicted=12 p50=30ms p95=220ms p99=980ms
[proxy] upstream read timeout at serve_worker.go:412
```

lucy_ops: Correlated proxy: a handful of 504 upstream read timeouts that line up with the p99 spikes. Also found a few 400s: \"dimension mismatch expected=1024 got=1536\" (trace tr-9ab3).

samuel_kwon: That explains a lot. If one request in a coalesced batch has a different embedding dim, the batcher either partially flushes or pads, which fragments batches and forces KV cache churn. Did the customer flip a partner variant recently?

alex_cheng: yes, partner rolled a new model and a minority of requests started coming back 1536-dim. Most traffic still 1024. My local repro:
1) hammer 200 requests with sleep 0.05s, varying input lengths
2) server dynbatch: max_batch_size=128, max_batch_wait_ms=100
Result: p50 ~30ms, p95 ~220ms, p99 spikes ~1s in a step pattern every few minutes.

maya_garcia: Any auth/billing anomalies? Retries could amplify the symptom.

alex_cheng: no 401s. Support picked up a billing spike from retries; customer flagged unexpected cost briefly.

support_bot: Alert: client org_8YxN reported embedding dimension mismatch. Last error: 400 dimension mismatch expected=1024 got=1536 (trace_id tr-9ab3)

lucy_ops: Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately:
- reduce max_batch_size to 64 for that tenant
- enable partial_batch_padding=true
- turn on prefer_slotting so similar shapes coalesce
I can roll the first two quickly and monitor.

samuel_kwon: In sims prefer_slotting + smaller max_batch_size cut p99 by ~2x on mixed-dim traffic. Also recommend pre-batch validation to reject or normalize mismatched dims before they pollute batches.

maya_garcia: Ops please proceed with the temp change and collect metrics for kv_eviction_rate and batch_fragmentation_ratio per-tenant.

lucy_ops: Rolled change at 2026-03-17T12:45:00Z: max_batch_size 128->64 for org_8YxN; enabled partial_batch_padding. Observed p99 drop from ~1s -> ~420ms within 5 minutes on affected hosts. KV evictions dropped ~2.8x.

alex_cheng: Confirmed. Logs show when 1536-dim requests hit, the batcher emitted \"partial_flush\" events and kv_evicted spiked. That lines up with the staircase tail pattern (periodic partner roll/traffic patterns).

samuel_kwon: Longer term action items:
- eng: implement pre-batch dim guard that returns a clear 400 and avoids mixing (owner: eng-ml)
- eng: batcher heuristic to avoid grouping different embedding dims and prefer slotting (owner: eng-runtime)
- infra: expose metrics per-tenant: batch_fragmentation_ratio and kv_eviction_rate (owner: eng-infra)

maya_garcia: Support actions: send the customer the repro steps, describe the temporary mitigation we applied, recommend they pin model dims or route variant to a different model name. Alex, can you own the customer comms?

alex_cheng: Yes. Drafting note now: root cause = intermittent partner variant sending 1536-dim embeddings while main stream is 1024 -> batch fragmentation + KV cache thrash -> tail p99 spikes and client retries -> billing blip. Mitigation performed: reduced max_batch_size and enabled padding; next steps: client to normalize dims, and we'll implement batching guards.

support_bot: Follow-up check scheduled 2026-03-17T13:30:00Z. Monitoring flag=true until then.

lucy_ops: Monitoring shows tail stabilized after changes. We'll keep tenant at reduced batch size until partner confirms a fix or we deploy slotting/guards. If they insist on high throughput with mixed dims, recommend a dedicated route for that variant.

alex_cheng: Thanks everyone. Leaving thread open for partner confirmation; will update once customer responds or when eng provides ETA on guards.
